passage:
Zainab's report card lay on the kitchen table, and she pushed it away. "Ms Fernandes gave me a low mark because she doesn't like me," she said. "The test was unfair. It's just my bad luck." She said the same thing about the spelling test, the drawing test and the sports day races. Each time her mother Disha, distracted by work calls, said, "We'll see," and moved on. Zainab stopped bringing up her results at all.

At school, the class teacher Jatin noticed that Zainab never tried the extra questions. "Why bother?" she said. "It happens or it doesn't." Jatin did not argue. He asked her to pick just five spelling words, practise them for a week and compare her score. Zainab got four out of five. She stared at the page as if it belonged to someone else.

That evening she said to Disha, quietly, "I practised, and it worked." Disha put down her phone and listened all the way through.

qa.q: How many of the five spelling words did Zainab get right?
qa.a: Zainab got four of the five words right.

qa.q: What connects Zainab's blaming of luck and teachers with her result on the five spelling words?
qa.a: Zainab says the low mark is bad luck and the test unfair, and skips the extra questions because it happens or it doesn't; after practising five spelling words she gets four out of five and says she practised and it worked. The small win shows her effort has an effect.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling when she said "Why bother?" to Jatin?
qa.a: Zainab felt discouraged and powerless, as if results simply happen to her.

qa.q: What did Disha do that helped Zainab?
qa.a: Disha put down her phone and listened all the way through, so Zainab felt heard instead of brushed off with "We'll see".

grounding: External locus of control in a child who blames luck, teachers and tests, and a small win that shows her effort has impact.
